newsitem.title: MEXICO: Iusacell seeks to block Telmex cable deal.
newsitem.headline: Iusacell seeks to block Telmex cable deal.

text.p: Mexico's cellular phone company Grupo Iusacell said on Thursday it and its subsidiary SOS Telecomunicaciones had formally opposed to the Federal Competition Commission Telefonos de Mexico's planned purchase of 51 percent of cable company Cablevision.

In a statement, Iusacell claimed that the deal would give "additional power" to Telmex's current monopoly in some parts of Mexico's telecommunications market, and that Cablevision should be owned by a Telmex competitor.
Telmex's ownership of Cablevision's cable network "could be used to grant wide-band transport service to large users, encouraging monopolistic practices," Iusacell said.
"Iusacell seeks to ensure that Cablevision is maintained independent of Telmex so that it becomes a competitor in basic local telefony and voice and data transport."
